# The Severed Lands

The Severed Lands is a real inhabited world of fortified towns, wilderness, ancient Warden works and landscapes fractured by violet tears called the Rift. Native-born people and newcomers build ordinary lives among its dangers. Some districts distrust arrivals; others welcome them. No single prejudice describes everyone.

Riftborn is the local name for transported arrivals, not a claim that they were born from the current wound. They often cannot remember the crossing, though names, skills and memories of earlier life can survive. Their SL-born children belong to this world and live and die here normally. The arrival phenomenon is older than the present crisis. What causes it and what happens at return are private truths in DM-SECRETS.md, not common knowledge.

The Rift's visible tears deform ground, displace buildings and affect wildlife. Scholars dispute its origin. Anchor installations contain disturbances; some include Door apertures that the Returners hope to use for passage home. Seven primary Warden Anchor stations are recorded, with destroyed, dark and missing stations and many lesser regulators. Waystation's dormant Door is the best-known intact aperture. A surviving regulator beneath Nexus is not an additional eighth primary station. Dead arches at the Cairnfields Door Graveyard were moved there after failure.

Thornwall is the fortified merchant town and first hub. Nexus is the larger cultural and scholarly city. Waystation is the Returners' mountain-pass refuge. The Cairnfields holds the Spire, Old Crane, dangerous raider territory and the Door Graveyard. Kell's Iron works the northern Hollows, whose displaced streets preserve people and records from earlier disasters. Use their existing location entries for public geography.

The Returners seek a way home; the Stayers build a local future. Neither desire is inherently corrupt. Reckless experiments, concealment, coercion and whose lives are placed at risk create the conflict. The Wardens' actual history and the safe procedure are discoverable facts, not an answer the GM invents at the climax.

In Rift Awakening the party begins with no special destiny: a sign, strangers waking beside them, danger on a road and a town willing to offer shelter. Their actions make them important. Public descriptions never reveal the crossing mechanism or treat this world's people as imaginary.
